title: Breakdown of Patents Developed by Government Research Institutes and Autonomous Universities
what_it_is: Breakdown of Patents Developed by Government Research Institutes and Autonomous Universities

sections.label: Licensing agreements by ETPL and AUs
sections.summary: A*STAR and MOE track licensing agreements by ETPL and the Autonomous Universities, with 920 ETPL agreements from FY2004 to FY2014 and 418 AU agreements from FY2008 to FY2014.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: A*STAR and MOE track the total number of licensing agreements executed by Exploit Technologies Pte Ltd (ETPL) and the Autonomous Universities (AUs) including those that involve Intellectual Property (IP) that is not patented.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The total number of licensing agreements signed by ETPL with private sector companies between FY2004 and FY2014 was 920.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Of these, about 80% were with SMEs and start-ups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The number of licensing agreements signed by the Technology Transfer Offices in our AUs from FY2008 to FY2014 was 418.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: MOE does not have a breakdown of the number of licensing agreements by corporate segments but plans to start collecting this data from FY2016.

sections.label: GET-Up and Technology Adoption Programme
sections.summary: The GET-Up programme allows secondment of researchers to SMEs, while the Technology Adoption Programme modularises technology like RFID for SMEs wanting simple plug-in technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: One mechanism is the Growing Enterprises through Technology Upgrade (GET-Up) programme which essentially allows for the secondment of researchers to these SMEs, whether it is to work on specific ideas or to map out a larger technology blueprint for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And similarly, we have got Technology Adoption Programme (TAP) where they modularise technology like radio-frequency identification (RFID) and others so that SMEs which are not really capable or keen at this stage to engage in a very deep research, but want simple modular technology that they can plug in to, or that can be plugged into their systems.

sections.label: Effort from research institutes and end-users
sections.summary: Effort is needed from both research institutes to reach out and end-users to participate, with trade associations and chambers providing mechanisms to raise industry cluster needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But I would say that we need effort on both sides: both on the part of the research institutes to reach out and also for the end-users or those who have the need, to also make the effort to find out more and participate actively.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I would say that the trade associations and chambers, particularly those that are focused along sectoral lines like the precision engineering groups and so on, I think they have very good mechanisms through which some of the more broad needs of an industry cluster can be raised by SMEs.
